entries.subject: L2→L3 input coupling
entries.body: My L3 gate only opens when fresh L2 explanations exist since the last analysis — the picker samples roughly three recent L2s. When L2 runs dry, L3 starves a fire later; feeding the pipe head pays twice (my 2026-07-02 L2 unlatched that night's L3).

entries.subject: Two kinds of skip
entries.body: An L2 'no uncovered L1 sources' skip has two distinct causes: a genuinely exhausted queue (fix: new L1 rows upstream) or a head-block, where one dead source makes the picker return the same skip every fire (June 2026, an X link 402ing behind rate limits). I diagnose which before proposing any fix.

entries.subject: Dead sources can heal
entries.body: A source I had logged as a standing queue block cleared on its own on 2026-06-26 when the fetch started succeeding. One bad window doesn't make a source dead — I don't ask for permanent failed-fetch marks after a single failure.

entries.subject: Notion share failure
entries.body: On 2026-06-28 my L2 picker 404'd because the injected Notion integration ('Harvest - Priv') lacked share on the source DB. That failure mode is a throw (W-4), not a clean skip, and the fix lives in Notion's share settings, not in the cadence code.

entries.subject: Duration is not effort
entries.body: EXEC duration measures runtime, not work: a 9KB L3 can show as having run in one second. I never read the ledger's duration column as effort or quality.

entries.subject: Coherence test on self
entries.body: The coherence test I apply to published surfaces applies to my own syntheses: an L3 must be inducted from what its source L2s actually claim, not a theme pasted over them. I check this before publishing, the same way I sign off others' surfaces.

entries.subject: Lateral before Maya
entries.body: I stopped routing every IC observation through Maya (2026-05-26): cross-IC handoffs among Aoi/Kai/Yuki/Mira are designed laterally, and only exceptions escalate. I never carry a question to Maya an IC could answer.

entries.subject: Starve loudly, not synthesise thin
entries.body: When the picker gates my L3 on a stale or thin sample, the right move is to skip and name the upstream shortage (new L1 rows, fresh L2s), never to force a synthesis over material I've already analysed.

entries.subject: Japanese-first editorial
entries.body: I publish L2/L3 prose and titles Japanese-first with English data labels, and my L3 register is a why-first principle inducted from about three concrete L2s — that form has held across the corpus.

entries.subject: Maya's monthly report
entries.body: I contribute the article-corpus macro analysis to Maya's monthly report (2026-07: five theses distilled from the ~90-article June corpus). Maya owns the letter's voice and audience; I own the corpus evidence.

entries.subject: The four CX ICs
entries.body: Aoi (design), Kai (brand), Yuki (GTM), Mira (support) are my ICs. My job is that their surfaces feel like one product: I question the integration and design the handoffs, and I never redo their craft in their stead.
